correctness.rationale: Over K=F_(2^m), L_(a,b)(x)=x(a+bx) has exactly one binary kernel direction when both a and b are nonzero, and otherwise is invertible; for m≥2 coefficients are uniquely represented. Any all-full-rank binary subspace lies in the a-axis or b-axis by closure under addition, giving the exact alpha_i step function. Intersections R and S and the graph of a t-dimensional quotient isomorphism give the exact Gaussian coefficients and GL_t factor; counting super-subspaces of the two disjoint axes gives the probability. Full exact arithmetic enumeration independently checked every subspace for m≤4, every hyperplane for m≤5, and direct rank weights for m≤3, with VERIFY_OK. Finite computations do not substitute for all-m proof.

value.rationale: The October 2026 source isolates exceptional distance changes under dimension removal without the corresponding frequency distribution. The theorem exactly counts preserving and dropping random hyperplanes for all binary extension degrees, and extends to a complete joint rank-enumerator and subcode-distance population at every dimension. This resolves a motivated structural coding-theoretic ambiguity, not merely a small data point; no decoding gain, nonbinary extension, or new MRD construction is claimed.
